title: AWS in Plain English: Accounts, Identity and Guardrails
summary: Understand AWS account boundaries, Organizations, IAM roles and temporary credentials before operating workloads.
plain_language_explanation: AWS security begins with account boundaries and identity. Organizations groups accounts, IAM controls permissions inside accounts, roles provide temporary credentials, and service control policies set organization-level guardrails without granting permissions by themselves.
quick_check: Why can an SCP permit an action while an IAM principal still cannot perform it?

title: AWS Organizations, IAM Roles and Least-Privilege Access
summary: Design multi-account governance and human/workload access without relying on broad long-lived credentials.
objective: Explain account governance, federated workforce access, temporary credentials, IAM roles and organization guardrails as separate but cooperating controls.
body_outline: Use multiple AWS accounts to separate workloads, environments and security boundaries under AWS Organizations.
Restrict use of the Organizations management account and avoid placing normal workloads there.
Prefer federation and IAM Identity Center for workforce users and temporary role credentials for human access.
Prefer IAM roles and temporary credentials for workloads instead of long-lived access keys.
Apply least privilege and regularly review unused identities, roles, policies and credentials.
Understand that SCPs and resource control policies constrain permissions but do not grant them.

title: Amazon VPC, Security Groups and Network ACL Boundaries
summary: Operate AWS network isolation by separating routing, stateful security groups and subnet-level network ACLs.
objective: Build a layered AWS networking mental model so routing, security groups, network ACLs and application health are diagnosed independently.
body_outline: A VPC provides an isolated virtual network with address ranges, subnets, routing and connectivity constructs.
Security groups are stateful controls associated with supported resources and should be scoped to required traffic.
Network ACLs operate at subnet level and provide stateless allow or deny filtering.
Separate route-table problems from security-group rules, network ACL rules, DNS resolution and target-service health.
Avoid broad internet exposure for administrative services and prefer controlled private connectivity or managed access patterns.
Treat internet gateways, NAT, transit connectivity, firewalls and load balancers as separate architectural layers.

title: AWS Operational Evidence: CloudWatch, CloudTrail and Change Attribution
summary: Connect metrics, logs, alarms and API audit history into an evidence-first operating model.
architecture_notes: AWS operations should separate service telemetry from audit evidence. CloudWatch provides metrics, logs and alarms for operational state, while CloudTrail records API activity for attribution and governance. Neither alone proves end-to-end application health. Incident work should correlate identity, account, Region, resource, time window and change history before remediation.
failure_modes: alarm exists but targets the wrong metric dimensions or Region
log group exists but the workload is not publishing expected logs
CloudTrail evidence is searched in the wrong account or Region
an SCP or IAM boundary is blamed before effective permissions are evaluated
security-group edits are attempted before route and network ACL evidence is checked
operators use root or long-lived keys for convenience during troubleshooting
a remediation succeeds technically but leaves no audit trail or post-condition evidence
enterprise_design_notes: Use centralized logging where appropriate, protect audit data, define alert ownership, retain evidence according to policy, and separate investigative credentials from mutation authority.

title: Read-Only AWS Governance, Network and Observability Evidence Pack
summary: Collect account, identity, VPC, security and monitoring evidence without changing AWS resources.
objective: Produce a timestamped AWS evidence pack before any IAM, organization, network or monitoring change is proposed.
steps: Confirm the approved AWS account, role and Region before collecting evidence.
Record caller identity and list relevant account or organization metadata only where permissions allow.
Inventory VPCs, subnets, route tables, security groups and network ACLs without editing them.
Inspect CloudWatch alarm metadata and selected log-group metadata without changing retention or alarm actions.
Query CloudTrail event history for the approved time window without altering trails or destinations.
Classify findings as identity, governance, routing, filtering, observability or workload-health issues before proposing remediation.
expected_result: A read-only AWS evidence pack showing caller identity, network controls and operational/audit telemetry with no resource mutation.
rollback: Not required; the prescribed commands are read-only.

title: AWS Access, Network or Observability Incident Decision Tree
summary: Separate AWS identity, organization, routing, filtering and telemetry failure domains before changing production controls.
diagnostic_order: Confirm account, assumed role, Region and resource identifiers before interpreting any result.
For access failures, distinguish authentication, IAM identity policy, resource policy, permissions boundary and Organizations guardrails.
For connectivity failures, prove address/subnet placement, route tables, security groups, network ACLs, DNS and target-service health separately.
For missing telemetry, prove metric/log source, Region, dimensions, log destination and alarm configuration before changing thresholds.
Use CloudTrail event history to correlate API actions and identity with the incident time window.
Escalate when remediation requires IAM changes, SCP changes, route/security-group/network-ACL changes, trail changes, resource restart or deployment.
escalation_boundary: Do not create access keys, elevate roles, change SCPs or IAM policies, edit routes/security groups/network ACLs, alter trails, modify alarm actions, restart resources or deploy fixes without approved change authority.

title: AWS Foundations and Operations Assessment
summary: Scenario assessment covering multi-account governance, IAM, VPC controls and operational evidence.

assessment_items.question: Does an SCP grant permissions to an IAM principal?
assessment_items.answer: No. SCPs define organization-level permission guardrails. Effective permissions still require applicable identity-based or resource-based permissions and must satisfy other policy boundaries.

assessment_items.question: Why are IAM roles preferred over long-lived access keys for workloads?
assessment_items.answer: Roles provide temporary credentials that reduce persistent credential exposure and can be scoped and rotated automatically.

assessment_items.question: What is the important operational difference between security groups and network ACLs?
assessment_items.answer: Security groups are stateful resource-level filters, while network ACLs are stateless subnet-level filters.

assessment_items.question: Why should CloudTrail and CloudWatch both be considered during an incident?
assessment_items.answer: CloudWatch helps show operational state through metrics, logs and alarms, while CloudTrail helps attribute API activity and changes to identities and time windows.

title: Senior AWS Interview: Governance, Networking and Evidence-First Operations
summary: Senior scenarios testing multi-account boundaries, least privilege, VPC diagnosis and auditability.

questions.question: A role has AdministratorAccess but an API call is denied. What do you inspect?
answer_points: check SCPs or other organization policies
avoid changing policies until the denying layer is proven

questions.question: An EC2 workload cannot reach an internal service. What layers do you prove before editing security groups?
answer_points: security groups on source and destination
